methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $50M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 5 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

private.name: Humanoid
private.rationale: Same sector (Robotics & Manufacturing), same stage (Series A), post-money $1.35B

data.narrative:
AIM Intelligent Machines is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $50M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies—spanning Series A through Seed stages—supplemented by reference to eight additional private and one public comparable (277810.KQ).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $50M raised as a valuation proxy, applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, yielding $100M. Peer-median analysis across five robotics peers (Generalist AI at $2.0B, Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B, Dexterity at $1.6B, Humanoid at $1.4B, and Walden Robotics at $1.1B) produces a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range from $1.1B to $2.0B.

These methods support a triangulated valuation range of $85M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $875M. The substantial spread reflects tension between stage-appropriate valuation based on capital deployed and peer comparables skewed upward by higher-stage funded peers. Key uncertainties include the extent to which peer-set stage heterogeneity (three Series B, one Series A, one Seed) applies to AIM's current position, and whether capital efficiency relative to peers justifies premium or discount positioning within the range.
